SECTION 1

* A 24-year-old person named Sam Webb is responding to comments made by politician Sajid Javid about young people and housing costs, saying that older people unfairly criticize millennials for spending money on things like vacations and dining out instead of saving for houses.

* Sam argues that even if young people saved every penny, they still couldn't afford to buy homes because house prices keep going up, there aren't enough houses available, and banks don't want to lend money as much as they used to.

* Sam feels frustrated that young people like him are stuck renting forever, paying money to property owners who then complain that young renters are being irresponsible with money.

* The second letter writer points out that people under 25 actually earn much less money than older workers - they don't get the full minimum wage and can be paid as little as £5.60-£7.05 per hour for doing the same work.

* Young workers are more likely to have unstable "zero-hours" contracts and might only earn around £14,500 per year even working full-time, making it nearly impossible to save enough money for a house deposit.
